back: The business is separate from its owner: only business transactions are recorded; private expenses paid by the business are drawings.
Every transaction has two equal aspects: a debit and a credit of the same amount.
Only items that can be measured reliably in money are recorded.
notes: So staff skills and customer loyalty are not shown as assets.

back: Assets are recorded at what they cost (including costs to get them ready for use), not at market value.
The business is assumed to continue for the foreseeable future, so assets are not valued at forced-sale prices.

front: When does going concern stop applying?
back: When the business is about to close; assets are then valued at what they would realise on sale.
Cost is objective and verifiable from documents; market values are subjective and change.

front: Which foundation concepts does ZIMSEC list?
back: Going concern, historical cost and double entry (duality).

front: Owner's private bill paid from the business bank
back: Debit drawings; credit bank (or move it from the expense account to drawings). It is not a business expense.
